# parity-fuzz --mode nest baseline: normalized signatures of KNOWN gaps.
# A divergence whose signature is here is allowed; a NEW one fails CI.
# Regenerate: parity-fuzz --mode nest --count N --verify 3  (copy NEW-signature lines).
#
# KNOWN GAP: inside `"…"`, an inner SET OPERATOR (`:|` difference, `:*`
# intersection) is still evaluated, where zsh has already collapsed the array to
# a scalar before the operator ever runs:
#
#   a=(one two three four); b=(two four six eight)
#   "${(j:,:)${a:|b}}"  -> zsh:   one two three four   (`:|` saw a SCALAR)
#                          zshrs: one,three            (`:|` saw the array)
#
# ROOT CAUSE (now understood, from Src/subst.c:2795-2801 in zsh 5.9.1):
#
#     if (isarr) {
#         if (nojoin) isarr = -1;
#         if (qt && !getlen && isarr > 0) { val = sepjoin(aval, sep, 1); isarr = 0; }
#     }
#
# C runs that collapse right after the nested multsub and BEFORE the operator
# dispatch (c:3433) and the sort block (c:4245). zshrs's port of the same rule
# fires in the right place for a DIRECTLY quoted expansion, but the nested-inner
# collapse added for the flag fix sits LATER in paramsubst — after the set-op
# arms — so `:|` still sees an array.
#
# Fix path: make the existing c:2798 site (subst.rs, `if qt && isarr > 0 &&
# spsep.is_none()`) also fire when SUBEXP_SCALAR_CTX > 0, and drop the late
# collapse. Attempted; the existing site is not reached for these shapes, so it
# needs the value/isarr initialisation order sorted out first.
#
# UNQUOTED forms match.
  print -r -- "[${(L)${(s.:.)${t[2]}}}]"
  print -r -- "[${#${#s}}]"
  print -r -- "[${${#${m#*_}}#*_}]"
